title: Why Bitcoin Matters
description: Money before Bitcoin: what it's for, where it fails for African users, and the five Bitcoin principles that turn every failure into a design problem.

objectives: Explain the three jobs of money and where born-into currencies quietly fail
Describe the four forces shaping money for African users — inflation, currency controls, remittances, mobile money
Explain why Bitcoin was created, in plain language, without jargon
Connect each of the five principles to a concrete design consequence

lesson.videoNote: Placeholder: Antonopoulos' Introduction to Bitcoin. Swap with Week 1 class recording when available.

resources.title: "Check Your Financial Privilege" — Alex Gladstein
resources.desc: The essay that reframes Bitcoin through the eyes of the 89% of the world not born into a reserve currency — with Nigeria's Feminist Coalition story. If you read one thing this week, read this.

resources.title: "What is Money, Anyway?" — Lyn Alden
resources.desc: The clearest long-form walk through what money is and how it breaks. Read the first half (through the fiat currency sections); stop when it turns to markets.

resources.title: Anita Posch — "Bitcoin Empowers Africa and Africans Empower Bitcoin"
resources.desc: Plan B Forum / BTC Prague keynote, ~25 min. First-hand field reporting from Zimbabwe, Zambia and beyond — watch it as design research: note actual behaviors, devices, and constraints, not just the message.

resources.title: Andreas Antonopoulos — "Introduction to Bitcoin"
resources.desc: ~30 min. The classic principles-first, price-free explanation of why Bitcoin is different in kind, not degree, from the money before it.

resources.title: The Little Bitcoin Book — Ajiboye, Gladstein, Song & others
resources.desc: Optional. ~120 pages, short and non-technical, co-written by a Nigerian builder — written around stories from Nigeria, Venezuela, and the Philippines. The best "give this to a friend" book in Bitcoin.
